A2.1 Network Fundamentals

Topic A2: Networks | Connecting Devices at Scale

Retrieval Practice

Quick recall from A1 before we start networks.

  1. What does the operating system manage when several apps run at once?
  2. What is the difference between bandwidth and latency?
  3. What is the key trade-off between interpretation and compilation?

Press Down for answers

Answer 1

What does the operating system manage when several apps run at once?

It allocates resources (CPU time, memory, devices/files) and enforces protection between processes.

Answer 2

What is the difference between bandwidth and latency?

Bandwidth is how much data per second; latency is the delay before data arrives.

Answer 3

What is the key trade-off between interpretation and compilation?

Interpreters give fast feedback but often slower runtime; compilers take longer upfront but often run faster.

The Big Question

🤔 You send a message from one phone to another…

and it arrives across the world in seconds.

What infrastructure makes that possible?

❌ Misconception: “The internet is just Wi‑Fi.”

Wi‑Fi is only one local technology; global connectivity is much bigger.

✅ Reality: networks are layered systems of devices, links, and protocols.

We classify networks by scale, and we measure them by speed and delay.

What is a Network?

Why connect computers instead of keeping everything on one machine?

A network connects devices so they can exchange data and share resources.

Benefits: communication, shared storage, shared hardware, distributed processing.

Core trade-off

Networks add capability, but also add complexity and security risk.

Network Types (By Range)

How far does your connection need to reach?
TypeTypical RangeKey Idea
PAN~10 mPersonal devices (Bluetooth, USB tethering)
LANBuilding/siteHigh bandwidth, low latency, shared local resources
WANCity → globalConnects LANs across distance
VPNAnySecure tunnel over public infrastructure

🧠 Quick Check

Bluetooth headphones connected to a phone are an example of which network type?

PAN — short-range personal network around one user.

Bandwidth vs Latency

Why can a connection download fast but still feel “laggy” in games?

Bandwidth is capacity (data per second).

Latency is delay (time to arrive).

Interactive tasks (gaming, calls) are sensitive to latency.

Intuition

Bandwidth is like “lane width”.

Latency is like “distance + traffic lights”.

🧠 Quick Check

For a real-time video call, which matters more: bandwidth or latency?

Latency (and jitter) largely determines how “responsive” the conversation feels.

Modern Infrastructure: Distributed Systems

What if we don’t want one “central computer” to be a single point of failure?

Distributed systems use many nodes working toward a shared goal.

They improve fault tolerance (no single point of failure).

The challenge

Maintaining consistency across many machines is difficult.

Edge Computing

Why process data near where it’s produced instead of sending everything to the cloud?

Edge computing moves compute closer to users/devices.

It reduces latency and reduces bandwidth load on core networks.

Example

Content providers (e.g., streaming) use local caching servers near users.

🔗 Connection to A4: many ML applications run at the edge (phones, cars) because decisions must be made with low latency.

Mobile Networks (5G)

What makes modern mobile networks suitable for “always-on” devices?

5G targets higher speeds and lower latency than earlier generations.

It supports the growth of IoT devices at large scale.

Why it matters

Low latency enables time-sensitive systems (industrial control, autonomous features).

Misconception Check

A. A VPN automatically makes you anonymous online.

B. LANs typically have lower latency than WANs.

C. Edge computing can reduce latency for users.

D. Distributed systems remove all reliability problems.

Press Down for answers

Answers

A: False. A VPN encrypts traffic to a VPN server; it does not guarantee anonymity.

B: True. WAN distance and routing usually increases delay.

C: True. Processing closer to the user reduces travel time.

D: False. They improve fault tolerance but introduce consistency/coordination challenges.

Key Takeaways

  • Networks connect devices to share resources and communicate.
  • We classify networks by scale: PAN, LAN, WAN, and VPN.
  • Bandwidth is capacity; latency is delay.
  • Modern services often use distributed systems and edge computing.
